healthcareSystem: US territory healthcare system. Schneider Regional Medical Center on St. Thomas and Governor Juan F. Luis Hospital on St. Croix are the main facilities. St. John has a small clinic. US FDA regulations apply. Medicare and Medicaid are accepted. US health insurance typically provides coverage.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is adequate for routine care and many emergencies, but not at mainland US standards. Hospitals have basic specialist services. English is the primary language. Complex cases are transferred to Puerto Rico or mainland US (Miami, Atlanta). Facilities were rebuilt after hurricane damage.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 9am-6pm weekdays, 9am-2pm Saturday. Some pharmacies in shopping areas may have extended hours. Closed Sundays and US holidays.
pharmacyTips: Standard US pharmacies are available on St. Thomas and St. Croix. US prescriptions are valid. Over-the-counter medications are the same as mainland US. St. John has more limited options — stock up before visiting.
prescriptionRules: US FDA regulations and prescription requirements apply. Valid US prescriptions are accepted at local pharmacies. Controlled substance rules follow DEA regulations.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled substances (Schedules I-V)
restrictedMeds.note: US DEA regulations apply. Must have valid US prescription. Keep in original pharmacy-labeled container.

bringDocumentation: Bring your US health insurance card and any prescription medications in original pharmacy-labeled containers. Standard US documentation applies. No special international requirements for US citizens.

travelInsurance.tips: US health insurance typically covers care in the USVI. Check your specific plan. Travel insurance is still recommended for trip cancellation and emergency evacuation to the mainland. Medicare covers some services. International visitors should have travel insurance.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required. Standard US vaccination recommendations apply. Zika and dengue have been reported — use insect repellent.

waterNotes: Tap water meets US EPA standards and is safe to drink on all three main islands. Water is primarily from desalination plants and cistern collection systems. Some visitors prefer bottled water for taste. Resort water is safe.
foodSafetyTips: US food safety standards and FDA regulations apply. Restaurant food is safe. Enjoy local specialties like conch fritters, johnnycakes, and fresh seafood. Standard food safety precautions apply as in the mainland US.
medicalTourismNote: The USVI is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing complex specialist care are transferred to Puerto Rico or mainland US hospitals.
sources: US Virgin Islands Department of Health
metaDescription: Health guide for US Virgin Islands: 911 emergency, pharmacies, US healthcare standards, insurance tips, and hospital info.

hospitals.name: Schneider Regional Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Main hospital on St. Thomas. Emergency department. Full-service hospital with most specialties. Nearest hospital to cruise port and resort areas.

hospitals.name: Governor Juan F. Luis Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital on St. Croix. Emergency department. Basic specialist services. Undergoing renovation and expansion.

hospitals.name: Myrah Keating Smith Community Health Center
hospitals.notes: Small community health center on St. John. Handles minor emergencies. Serious cases transferred to St. Thomas by ferry or helicopter.

dentalCare.availability: Good. Multiple private dental practices on St. Thomas and St. Croix.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care meets US standards. Several private practices on each major island. US dental insurance may be accepted. Costs are similar to mainland US.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, private dental offices on St. Thomas and St. Croix can usually accommodate walk-ins or same-day appointments.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Multiple English-speaking mental health professionals available on St. Thomas and St. Croix
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available through the USVI Department of Health and private practitioners. The 988 Lifeline is accessible. Telehealth options are also available.

accessibilityInfo.overview: ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) applies in the USVI. Accessibility is improving but not at mainland US standards.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transit (VITRAN buses) has limited accessibility. Paratransit services available. Taxis and rental cars are the primary transport.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Major tourist areas and resorts generally meet ADA standards. Historic areas in Charlotte Amalie have steep hills and stairs. Beaches vary in accessibility. Contact specific attractions in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask requirements. Follow CDC guidelines for personal protection.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at hospitals and some pharmacies.
covidStatus.notes: US COVID protocols and CDC guidelines apply. Hospitals can treat COVID cases.

insuranceClaimProcess: Standard US insurance billing process. Hospitals accept most US insurance plans, Medicare, and Medicaid. Provide your insurance card at registration. Co-pays and deductibles apply per your plan. Out-of-network charges may apply for some mainland plans — verify with your insurer.

commonCosts.note: Costs are similar to mainland US. Insurance accepted at most facilities. Uninsured patients should expect US-level pricing.

medicalEvacuation.note: Air ambulance to Puerto Rico or mainland US is available. US Coast Guard assists with maritime emergencies. St. John patients are transferred to St. Thomas first. Insurance coverage for medical flights recommended.
